repaired.name: Scenario
repaired.script:
triggered := false
if (triggered == true) {
    wait until(not (all(#LightSensor).lightSensor_brightness <| 50))
    triggered = false
}
wait until(all(#LightSensor).lightSensor_brightness <| 50)
all(#WindowCovering).windowCovering_upOrOpen()
triggered = true

diagnosis.summary: The IR implements a rising-edge wait (fire once when condition transitions true, then wait for false before next fire). The candidate uses a periodic `if` which only checks the condition at the start of every 1-second iteration. At t=100ms, the condition became true (Light_S.brightness=0), but the candidate's `if` guard evaluated to false because it was only checked at t=0 when brightness was null. The rising edge occurred between iterations, so the candidate missed the event.
diagnosis.change_summary: Replaced the periodic `if` polling with a blocking two-wait rearming pattern. The script now blocks until the condition is true (rising edge), executes the action, then blocks until the condition is false before the next cycle can start. This matches the IR's `wait(cond, edge rising)` semantics.
